claims.text: As-processed HfZrTiTa0.53 has a yield strength of approximately 786 MPa.
As-processed HfZrTiTa0.53 has a compressive strength of approximately 1314 MPa.
As-processed HfZrTiTa0.53 has limited tensile ductility.
Severe plastic deformation followed by partial annealing will produce a bimodal grain-size distribution in HfZrTiTa0.53.
The proposed bimodal structure will significantly improve the tensile ductility of HfZrTiTa0.53.
The proposed bimodal structure will significantly improve the uniform tensile elongation of HfZrTiTa0.53.
Partial annealing after severe plastic deformation will form a coarse-grained fraction while retaining a fine-grained fraction.
Coarser grains will enhance dislocation mobility in treated HfZrTiTa0.53.
The coarse-grained fraction will generate back-stress hardening.
Enhanced dislocation activity and back-stress hardening will delay tensile necking and improve uniform elongation.
The retained fine-grained fraction will preserve the alloy's yield strength.
The retained fine-grained fraction will preserve the alloy's compressive strength.
The retained fine-grained fraction will preserve impact-triggered energy release.
Treated HfZrTiTa0.53 will exhibit uniform tensile elongation exceeding 20% at room temperature.
Treated HfZrTiTa0.53 will retain a yield strength near 786 MPa.
Treated HfZrTiTa0.53 will retain a compressive strength near 1314 MPa.
Treatment will not degrade the impact-triggered energy-release performance of HfZrTiTa0.53.
The hypothesis is scoped to room-temperature quasi-static tension at approximately 10^-3 s^-1.
Matched compression, tension, impact, and microstructural tests can compare treated material with a conventionally processed control.

contradictions.description: The prediction requires elongation exceeding 20%, whereas the falsification rule requires elongation significantly above 20%; an outcome only slightly above 20% could satisfy the prediction yet be declared falsifying.

Yield strength is predicted only to remain near 786 MPa, but the falsification rule rejects any value below approximately 786 MPa; values slightly below 786 MPa could reasonably be 'near' the prediction while also meeting the stated falsification condition.
